title: ASAS-SN g eclipses of TYC 9179-1083-1 (2018-2025) occur at the published three-body times and are 0.56 +- 0.15 of the TESS depth; this agrees with a cool eclipsed star and a hotter, dominant tertiary
abstract: A campaign study found a third star on a 5.9-year orbit around the eccentric 10.29-day eclipsing binary TYC 9179-1083-1 from TESS eclipse times. Later studies disagree about which star gives most of the light. One GALAH spectrum shows a hot, dominant tertiary and a cool eclipsed star with about 17 percent of the light. All these studies use TESS photometry in one band. We tested this with ASAS-SN Sky Patrol photometry (V 2014-2018, g 2018-2025; 4,534 points), an independent instrument in a bluer band. We fixed the eclipse times to the published three-body model, recomputed with the source code (0.385 min rms against the TESS primary times). ASAS-SN g detects the primary eclipses at these times (null p-value 0.0075 from 400 random time shifts). A common time shift is -3 min (1-sigma -12 to +3 min). The g depth is R = 0.56 +- 0.15 of the TESS depth at the same time (28 in-eclipse points; error from the null shifts). Blackbody band light, limb darkening and the published geometry predict R = 0.46-0.78 for the GALAH light model and 0.88-0.98 if the eclipsed star gives most of the light. Thus the measurement agrees with a cool eclipsed star and a hotter, dominant tertiary, and is 2.2 sigma below the dominant-eclipsed-star case. The V data have only 6 eclipse points and cannot test the start of the eclipse window. Limits: few eclipse points, a moderate 2-sigma result, blackbody and approximate limb-darkening models, and unmodelled blending in the ASAS-SN aperture.

display.caption: ASAS-SN g primary eclipses at the model times with the TESS depth (red) and the fit (blue, R = 0.56); measured depth ratio against the expected ranges for the two light models; chi-square against a common shift of the model eclipse times.
Primary eclipse depth: TESS trend and the ASAS-SN depths implied by the fitted ratios. The 2014-2018 V point has a large error and does not test the start of the eclipse window.
